The `PromptTokenizer` implements bounded token reuse by identifying literal message boundaries within the input text. It searches for a specific end-of-message marker, treating the text preceding this marker as a prefix for caching purposes. This approach allows the system to avoid re-tokenizing identical historical context, thereby optimizing generation speed when prompts contain repeated segments.

Cache eligibility is strictly governed by length and configuration. The system only attempts to cache prefixes that exceed a minimum character threshold, ensuring that small variations do not trigger unnecessary lookups. Furthermore, caching is disabled if the underlying tokenizer does not support literal boundary splitting or if the prefix is too short to justify the overhead. The system verifies that the marker is not consumed by other added tokens, ensuring that the cached tokens accurately represent the text up to the boundary.

Storage limits are enforced through a budget-based LRU cache that tracks both the number of entries and the byte size of stored prefixes. Each entry maps a text prefix to its corresponding token IDs, serialized as a byte array. The cache automatically evicts older entries when the total size exceeds the defined budget, balancing memory consumption against the potential for token reuse. This ensures that the cache remains efficient without consuming excessive system resources.

Thread safety is maintained using a lock to protect concurrent access to the cache
